jobs.title: 12Y Geospatial Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description

You can play an important part in disaster relief missions as a Geospatial Engineer for the Army National Guard. In this role, you will extract and supply geographic data that supports military operations of all kinds and help commanders visualize the battlefield during combat.

As a Geospatial Engineer, your primary responsibility will be to collect and process military geographic information from decentralized sources (remote sensed imagery, digital data, intelligence data, existing topographic products, and other collateral data sources), present this information to leaders, and return decisions to the field.

You May Also

Supervise topographic surveying, cartography, and photolithography activities
Assist in topographic planning and control activities
Assist in determining requirements and providing technical supervision of geographic intelligence programs

Job Duties

Create geographic data and compile them into maps
Create and maintain multiple geospatial databases
Prepare military-style briefs covering all aspects of the terrain

Some Of The Skills You’ll Learn

Basic knowledge of Geographic Information Systems
Imagery interpretation and exploitation

Helpful Skills

Interest in geography, maps, and charts
Ability to demonstrate basic computer skills and work with drafting equipment
Conceptualize ideas into computer-generated 2-D/3-D geospatial products
Preference for a technical career field

Through your training, you will develop the skills and experience to enjoy a civilian career with construction, engineering, and architectural firms, as well as with government agencies as a surveyor, mapmaker, cartographer, cartographic technician, or photogrammetrist.

Earn While You Learn

Instead of paying to learn these skills, get paid to train. In the Army National Guard, you will learn these valuable job skills while earning a regular paycheck and qualifying for tuition assistance.

Job training for a Geospatial Engineer requires 10 weeks of Basic Training, where you'll learn basic Soldiering skills, and 20 weeks of Advanced Individual Training (AIT) and on-the-job instruction, including practical application of geographic information systems. Part of this time is spent in the classroom and part in the field.

Benefits/Requirements

Benefits

Paid training
A monthly paycheck
Montgomery GI Bill
Federal and State tuition assistance
Retirement benefits for part-time service
Low-cost life insurance (up to $400,000 in coverage)
401(k)-type savings plan
Student Loan Repayment Program (up to $50,000, for existing loans)
Health care benefits available
VA home loans
Bonuses, if applicable
Most non-prior service candidates will earn between $200 and $250 per drill weekend, subject to change

Requirements

Military enlistment in the Army National Guard
Must be at least a junior in high school, or have a high school diploma or a GED certificate
Must be between the ages of 17 and 35
Must be able to pass a physical exam and meet legal and moral standards
Must meet citizenship requirements (see NATIONALGUARD.com for details)

jobs.title: Senior GIS Developer
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior GIS Developer based in United States.

The Senior GIS Developer will build and support GIS solutions that enable complex business and network operations.

The role combines advanced GIS expertise with strong software-development and automation capabilities.

You will work across QGIS, ArcGIS, enterprise databases, web technologies, and spatial data systems.

Your work will support mapping, network analysis, data management, and operational workflows at scale.

You will also contribute to GIS architecture, standards, system integrations, and innovative tooling.

The position offers an opportunity to collaborate within an Agile/Scrum environment on highly impactful geospatial solutions.

Strong technical judgment, analytical thinking, and attention to data quality will be essential to success.

Accountabilities

Design, develop, and support server-based geoprocessing tools and automated data-update processes using Python and SQL, helping streamline recurring GIS operations and improve data reliability.
Build, deploy, maintain, and enhance custom QGIS plugins and forms using Python, PyQGIS, and Qt-based interfaces to support data acquisition, editing, validation, geoprocessing, and integration with other systems.
Partner with GIS engineering leadership to advance custom GIS tools, system integrations, and solution architecture, while contributing to architecture diagrams and technical design decisions.
Design and implement organization-wide GIS standards across server, cloud, web, desktop, and enterprise database environments to promote consistency, scalability, and maintainability.
Build and maintain FME Flow or Python-based ETL and scheduled data-processing workflows that automate mapping, data management, and recurring GIS activities.
Develop and maintain network-routing solutions using shortest-path algorithms while accounting for complex dependencies, constraints, spatial relationships, and business requirements.
Produce technical documentation, coding standards, workflow guidance, and training materials, while supporting knowledge transfer through demonstrations and remote training sessions.
Contribute throughout the software-development lifecycle within an Agile/Scrum team, collaborating with technical and business stakeholders to deliver reliable GIS capabilities.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Computer Science, or a closely related discipline, supported by a strong understanding of geographic concepts and principles, along with 5–7 years of relevant GIS and software-development experience.
Advanced Python skills applied to GIS automation, geoprocessing, ArcGIS web applications, REST services, and network-analysis workflows, with strong SQL and relational database experience, preferably including PostgreSQL/PostGIS.
Strong knowledge of Esri ArcGIS technologies, including desktop, online, server, enterprise databases, vector data, geoprocessing, and spatial-analysis capabilities, combined with hands-on QGIS and PyQGIS experience.
Practical experience creating QGIS plugins, custom processing tools, forms, or workflow extensions, as well as experience with FME-based or Python-driven ETL and automated processing workflows.
Strong web-development capabilities using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with experience working with ArcGIS JavaScript APIs, Web AppBuilder, ArcGIS Server services, REST APIs, and other integration technologies.
Solid understanding of software-development lifecycle practices, source control, testing, debugging, maintainable code design, algorithms, data structures, data modeling, and distributed systems, particularly as applied to spatial and network problems.
Strong knowledge of vector data, geoprocessing, spatial analysis, coordinate systems, topology, and network-routing concepts, supported by excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.
Experience designing or consuming APIs and integrating GIS platforms with external business or operational systems, with strong attention to accuracy, data quality, and technical detail.
Experience in telecommunications, outside plant (OSP), fiber network inventory, route planning, network design, or other comparable network-oriented environments is highly valuable.
Demonstrated ability to lead user training, develop technical process documentation, support GIS users across multiple teams, and communicate complex technical concepts effectively.

Benefits

Estimated annual base salary of $95,100–$146,300 USD, with actual compensation determined by factors such as geographic location, experience, skills, certifications, and organizational needs.
Potential eligibility for a discretionary annual incentive plan for non-sales roles.
Excellent health, dental, and vision insurance.
Retirement savings through a 401(k) plan.
Generous paid time off, including paid parental leave.
Remote work opportunity within the United States.
Opportunity to work on large-scale GIS, network, spatial-data, automation, and systems-integration initiatives.

jobs.title: Environmental Compliance Specialist I
jobs.description:
Aqua, an Essential Utilities company, employs people in a variety of roles within our eight-state footprint, ranging from field workers and customer service representatives who are on the front lines working with customers, to scientists and engineers who help ensure we’re delivering reliable water and wastewater services to our communities. If you’re looking for a rewarding career helping improve our environment and protect our natural resources, we encourage you to join our team!

About Essential Utilities

Essential Utilities, Inc. delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities.

Operating as the Aqua (water and wastewater services) and the Peoples and Delta (natural gas) brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across 10 states. We are committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status - including a competitive and comprehensive benefits package as well as a commitment to career growth opportunities.

We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting more than 7,600 acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint.

Our company is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Conducts leak detection investigations and system surveys of Aqua‑owned water and wastewater facilities, distribution mains, service lines, hydrants, valves, and related infrastructure to identify real water losses, unaccounted‑for water, and potential infrastructure failures.
Performs or supports acoustic, pressure, flow, and meter data analysis to assist with leak location, verification, and prioritization of repairs.
Coordinates with Operations, Engineering, and outside contractors during leak detection surveys, field investigations, and corrective actions.
Documents findings from leak detection activities, prepares summary reports, and enters results into tracking systems or databases to support asset management and regulatory reporting.
Assists with investigation and response to customer complaints related to suspected leaks, pressure concerns, or unexplained water usage.
Supports water loss control initiatives by collecting field data used for water audits, system evaluations, and infrastructure improvement planning.
Issues work orders or repair recommendations based on identified leaks or system deficiencies and tracks corrective actions to completion.
Participates in field work associated with emergency response, system failures, or regulatory inquiries related to water loss or distribution system integrity.
Schedules sampling for all systems at the appropriate times and assists operators and managers with sampling issues. Records and monitors test results on Excel or database spreadsheets. Contacts the state to correct any discrepancies. Ensures compliance with sampling requirements by reviewing chain of custody forms, checks sample codes, and works with the labs to ensure complete and accurate paperwork for each sample and track sample results. Ensures that all monthly and quarterly samples are collected. Reviews the test results for compliance. Reports any exceeding amounts to the responsible departments (internal managers).
Drafts compliance reports and compiles data for reports. Organizes and tracks compliance work for inclusion in reports, including field data. Issues work orders and schedules for additional compliance work. Plots and graphs data, and tracks compliance. Ensures timely preparation and filing of all compliance reports and permits.
Reviews inspection reports and regulatory correspondence. Shares information with others electronically and drafts response letters. Issues work orders for compliance repairs. Meets with operators and managers to discuss inspection reports. Works with engineer and managers to draft responses.
Coordinates, drafts, and issues any public notices as required working with management, engineering, and staff.
Assists in the resolution or response to compliance.
Prepares and maintains sampling plans including monthly bacteriological, lead and copper, disinfection by-products, and others for all systems and updates sample sites as needed. Ensures all samples are collected and reviews data.
Answers customer inquiries regarding analysis results and distributing copies of results if needed. Provides administrative support to Engineering Department. Processes invoices, copy, route and file documents as needed.
Prepares reports and tracks progress of budgeted project work.
Participates in meetings and other activities of Aqua as required.
Collects data from flow recorder data recorders and pressure recorders. Downloads data to PC and plot data.
Assists in the development of operating and capital budgets. Assists with permit reviews, renewals, and special or new monitoring requirements.
Provides input and assistance with preliminary design, project management, and contractor coordination for compliance-related capital projects, as needed.
Communicate urgent information to supervisors and operators and customers regarding water quality inquiries. Serve in an advisory/training capacity towards plant staff on sampling and proper test procedures to ensure compliance.
Performs other assignments as required.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Activities, duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

Education Requirements

Associate Degree; Bachelor’s degree preferred

Specialized Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of water distribution systems, leak detection principles, and water loss control concepts preferred.
Ability to interpret flow, pressure, and acoustic data from field monitoring equipment.
Ability to perform field investigations under varying weather and site conditions.

Professional Certification and Licenses

Ohio EPA Water Distribution II license or the ability to obtain the license within 2 years of employment.

Experience Level

1–2 years of related experience (environmental compliance, water distribution, leak detection, or utility field work preferred).

Office Technology Level

Competent to use Microsoft Office suite: Word‚ PowerPoint and Excel.

Communication Skills

Uses skills needed to obtain or provide routine information and answer some routine and technical questions; Communication often requires some interpretation (e.g. dealing with inquiries).

Driver’s License Required

Yes

Overall Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle or feel and reach with hands and arms.

Field work may require extended walking, standing, and working in uneven terrain, roadway environments, vaults, or excavation areas while performing leak detection surveys and investigations.

jobs.title: Senior BIM Engineer - Geo Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

The suitable candidate for this role is a Senior BIM Engineer specialising in Geo-Environmental, Civil infrastructure projects, with a strong focus on digital delivery and Civil 3D modelling. The role involves close coordination with design engineers and multidisciplinary teams across India and global regions, supporting project delivery through high-quality CAD and 3D modelling outputs.

The Senior BIM Engineer will take ownership of 3D modelling, drafting, and preparation of design documentation for Geo-Environmental, civil infrastructure, including water supply, wastewater, stormwater systems, and utility networks. The role supports projects across all stages, from concept and preliminary design through to detailed design and construction documentation.

Key responsibilities include developing and maintaining Civil 3D models (surfaces, alignments, corridors, pipe networks), integrating GIS and survey data, ensuring QA/QC compliance, and delivering accurate, coordinated, and construction-ready digital deliverables aligned with project standards and client expectations.

Responsibilities

RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop, review, and maintain high-quality 2D and 3D CAD models and drawings for Geo-Environmental, civil infrastructure projects, ensuring accuracy and compliance with project requirements, Australian standards, and company guidelines.
Produce and manage detailed 3D civil models in Autodesk Civil 3D, including surfaces, alignments, profiles, corridors, grading, and utility models.
Prepare accurate engineering drawings and documentation, including plans, sections, long sections, details, and construction drawings suitable for tender and construction stages.
Manage and process spatial/geospatial data (GIS/CAD) to support design development, analysis, and project documentation workflows.
Coordinate closely with engineers, designers, and multidisciplinary teams to ensure design intent, technical standards, and project requirements are fully achieved.
Lead the coordination and integration of digital design models across disciplines (civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical) to ensure clash-free and constructible solutions.
Maintain and enforce CAD/BIM standards, naming conventions, and modelling best practices, ensuring consistency and quality across deliverables.
Perform quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) checks and audits of drawings and models in line with project specifications, company standards, and client requirements.
Support data exchange and interoperability workflows, including GIS/CAD integration, model sharing, and preparation of digital deliverables for clients and contractors.
Collaborate with project stakeholders (engineers, architects, project managers, and external partners) to resolve design issues, improve efficiency, and optimise design solutions.
Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and support to junior modellers and drafters, promoting knowledge sharing and capability development within the team.
Develop and maintain CAD libraries, templates, and standard details to enhance productivity, consistency, and efficiency across projects.
Participate in design reviews and project meetings, contributing technical input on modelling strategies, constructability, and digital delivery approaches.
Manage multiple project deliverables simultaneously, prioritising tasks effectively to meet deadlines while maintaining a high standard of quality.

Bring your curiosity and determination to make a positive impact on the future of mining!
Together and with our mining clients, we will create a lasting community benefit making water, energy, and communities sustainable for generations to come.

Be a project manager delivering services to our mining clients.
Work on exciting mining projects for new and existing clients. Showcase your technical capabilities and expertise.

Join GHD.

Who are we looking for?

GHD’s U.S West Mining Team is seeking a motivated Project Manager
to join our Mining Team and support the planning, execution, and delivery of legacy mine reclamation and remediation projects. This role is ideal for a technically skilled professional with approximately five years of industry experience who is ready to transition into project management. Working under the guidance of senior project managers, the successful candidate will coordinate project activities, support client communications, manage schedules and budgets, and help deliver projects safely, on time, and within budget.

Our Hybrid Work Model
: Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Initiate and plan projects using disciplined project management practices (scope confirmation, WBS, schedule, risk planning, onboarding).
Manage execution and controls: track progress, issues, changes, and dependencies; maintain project records in the project workspace for traceability.
Coordinate communications and reporting cadence; maintain deadline control for regulatory and client reporting obligations.
Manage vendors and subcontractors under defined procedures; ensure work plans and outputs follow required verification pathways.
Support digital field data collection and standardized reporting workflows; contribute to dashboards and evidence packs used for program and project visibility.
Prepare deliverables and ensure they are ready for check/review with project director and/or subject matter expert approval prior to external use.
Escalate risks and deviations early using leading indicators and agreed thresholds to support ‘no surprises’ delivery.
Close out projects with complete documentation, lessons learned, and handoff as required

Demonstrated experience in leading environmental field data collection, soil & groundwater investigations, and technical report preparation programs.
Ability to manage scope, schedule, cost, and risk with a structured approach.
Strong coordination skills across field/office resources, and multi-disciplinary technical teams.
Clear written and verbal communication skills; capable of producing and managing recurring reporting deliverables.
Ownership and follow-through on commitments
Strong attention to detail
Effective communication with technical and non-technical audiences
Collaborative relationships with clients and team members.
Leadership potential and a desire to grow into larger project management responsibilities
A balance of technical problem-solving with business and project objectives.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Civil, Geological, Geotechnical, Environmental, or Mining Engineering, or related field
Approximately 5+ years of technical experience in environmental remediation and site assessments, report writing, data management & interpretation, project coordination, and managing clients.
Project management experience is required beyond day-to-day task management (e.g., defining project scope/objectives, establishing and monitoring budgets, allocating resources, anticipating/mitigating risks).
Understanding of project management principles and methodologies required
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines required.
Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills required.
Prior experience coordinating projects, task teams, and technical work packages required
Exposure to project budgeting, scheduling, forecasting, or client management preferred
Exposure to project management systems such as project accounting software (e.g., BST, Deltek, etc.), MS Project, and/or Primavera P6 preferred,
Experience in remediation and reclamation of legacy mine sites preferred.
CERCLA, RCRA, and/or state-led remediation program experience a plus.
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification desired
MSHA 24-hour New Miner training desired, but not required
Ability and willingness to travel to client meetings is required
PE a plus, but not required

jobs.description:
Career Area

Environmental Health and Safety

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Caterpillar is developing a new advanced manufacturing campus in Sanford, North Carolina, to expand production capacity for compact track loaders and telehandlers. The modern, technology-enabled operation is expected to incorporate automation, robotics, digital production systems and integrated logistics capabilities to enhance safety, quality and operational performance. Employees will help build the products our customers rely on while developing skills in advanced manufacturing and supporting the continued growth of Caterpillar’s Cat Compact℠ business.

Job Summary

The Environmental, Health and Safety Manager will provide site-level EHS leadership for a new advanced manufacturing facility, helping the site launch safely and build strong operating discipline from the beginning. This leader will be involved from construction planning through startup and stable production. Early priorities will include contractor evaluation related to safety, safety training, contractor safety program adherence, construction risk, site controls and readiness.

This role supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture, where safety is not a checklist or a set of procedures. It requires an EHS leader who can lead through ambiguity, influence project and operations leaders, work directly with contractors and employees, and build a safety culture where safe behavior is coached, expected and reinforced in the flow of daily work.

What You Will Do

Lead EHS execution for a new advanced manufacturing site from construction planning through startup.
Set clear construction-phase safety expectations for contractors, project teams and site leaders, including orientation, site access, work planning, hazard controls, inspections and corrective actions.
Build practical EHS programs, training, audits, reporting routines and risk-reduction processes that support Caterpillar standards, legal requirements and local operating needs.
Partner with construction, facilities, operations, engineering, maintenance, security, human resources, suppliers, contractors and system integrators to identify risks early and resolve issues quickly.
Support safe implementation of advanced manufacturing systems, automated material movement, connected equipment, robotics, energy systems, utilities and production processes.
Establish leader routines for hazard identification, risk assessment, contractor safety, incident response, corrective actions and emergency preparedness.
Use EHS data, leading indicators, inspections, observations, incident trends and audit findings to guide decisions and focus resources where risk is highest.
Provide leadership for environmental compliance, waste management, chemical management, air, water, stormwater, permitting and sustainability-related programs.
Coach leaders and employees, using field observations, feedback, leader routines and follow-up to reinforce safe decisions during construction and startup.

What You Will Have

Environmental Health and Safety Policy Compliance:
Knowledge of environmental, health and safety policies, standards, procedures and legal requirements; ability to lead programs that protect employees, contractors, visitors in a manufacturing environment.

Risk Management:
Knowledge of tools, approaches and practices for identifying, assessing, controlling and monitoring operational, environmental, construction and occupational-health risks before they become incidents.

Decision Making and Critical Thinking:
Ability to analyze technical, operational and compliance data, evaluate alternatives, assess risk and make sound recommendations. Ability to manage multiple priorities while balancing safety, compliance, schedule, cost and operational impact.

Project Management:
Ability to plan, organize, monitor and deliver EHS-related projects, launch activities, corrective actions and readiness plans to scope, schedule and quality expectations. Ability to work with cross-functional teams.

Safety Culture Leadership:
Ability to influence how leaders, employees and contractors think about risk, speak up about hazards, correct unsafe conditions and make safe choices in daily work.

Top Candidates Will Also Have

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health and Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Manufacturing, Construction Management.
Relevant EHS professional certification, such as CSP, ASP, CHMM, CIH, OSHA 30, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 or a comparable credential.
Experience improving EHS performance through both practical processes and behavior-based safety approaches.
Experience supporting construction safety, contractor safety, facility startup, capital projects, commissioning or major operational change.
Experience identifying hazards, assessing risk, implementing controls, investigating incidents and tracking corrective actions.
Strong communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills.

What You Will Get

Launch a new advanced manufacturing operation and shape the EHS foundation from construction through start up.
Lead work that supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture and reinforces that safety is how the work gets done.
Play a visible leadership role in shaping how a new site operates from day one.
Help implement practical EHS systems that support automation, advanced manufacturing, and safe production.

Additional Info

Location: Sanford, North Carolina
Work Arrangement: Onsite, five days per week. Locations may flex between temporary offices while transitioning to new facility.
Travel: High percentage of travel (50-75%) may be required at certain times during construction planning, supplier reviews, equipment installation, commissioning, startup and production ramp-up.
Schedule: This will be a demanding and very rewarding role. Selected candidate should have schedule flexibility to meet project requirements.
Relocation: US domestic relocation is available
Visa Sponsorship: Not available

Summary Pay Range

$128,470.00 - $192,710.00

Compensation and benefits offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, job level, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, individual performance and experience. Please note that salary is only one component of total compensation at Caterpillar.

Role Overview

Serves as the Pollution Control Officer (PCO) for the Research compound, overseeing regulatory compliance and permitting activities.
Prepares, processes, and renews environmental and regulatory permits, licenses, and clearances, including but not limited to:
DENR-EMB (e.g., ECC, Discharge Permits, Hazardous Waste Generator ID, PTO, SQI, PMPIN, PCL, CCO)
DOLE (e.g., Permit to Operate, Certificate of Electrical Safety Inspection)
Other agencies: LGUs, BFP, PDEA, PNP, ERC as required

Coordinates with regulatory bodies and government agencies for inspections, compliance audits, and reporting.
Maintains accurate and up-to-date records of permits, inspections, laboratory results and compliance documentation

Oversees environmental performance of the Research Compound including air emissions, wastewater, hazardous and solid waste, and chemical storage and use compliance by:
coordinating environmental monitoring and pollution control activities
monitoring wastewater treatment plant (WWTP/STP) operations
ensuring proper handling, storage and disposal of hazardous substances and chemicals (including development of Chemical Management Plans)
ensuring compliance in the use of PNP and PDEA related controlled chemicals

Prepares, submits and files/documents the following in a timely manner:
Self monitoring reports (SMRs)
Compliance monitoring reports (CMRs)
Priority Chemicals List (PCL) reports
SQI-related chemical consumption reports

Essential Utilities, Inc. delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities.

Operating as the Aqua (water and wastewater services) and the Peoples and Delta (natural gas) brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across 10 states. We are committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status - including a competitive and comprehensive benefits package as well as a commitment to career growth opportunities.

Our company is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Conducts leak detection investigations and system surveys of Aqua‑owned water and wastewater facilities, distribution mains, service lines, hydrants, valves, and related infrastructure to identify real water losses, unaccounted‑for water, and potential infrastructure failures.
Performs or supports acoustic, pressure, flow, and meter data analysis to assist with leak location, verification, and prioritization of repairs.
Coordinates with Operations, Engineering, and outside contractors during leak detection surveys, field investigations, and corrective actions.
Documents findings from leak detection activities, prepares summary reports, and enters results into tracking systems or databases to support asset management and regulatory reporting.
Assists with investigation and response to customer complaints related to suspected leaks, pressure concerns, or unexplained water usage.
Supports water loss control initiatives by collecting field data used for water audits, system evaluations, and infrastructure improvement planning.
Issues work orders or repair recommendations based on identified leaks or system deficiencies and tracks corrective actions to completion.
Participates in field work associated with emergency response, system failures, or regulatory inquiries related to water loss or distribution system integrity.
Schedules sampling for all systems at the appropriate times and assists operators and managers with sampling issues. Records and monitors test results on Excel or database spreadsheets. Contacts the state to correct any discrepancies. Ensures compliance with sampling requirements by reviewing chain of custody forms, checks sample codes, and works with the labs to ensure complete and accurate paperwork for each sample and track sample results. Ensures that all monthly and quarterly samples are collected. Reviews the test results for compliance. Reports any exceeding amounts to the responsible departments (internal managers).
Drafts compliance reports and compiles data for reports. Organizes and tracks compliance work for inclusion in reports, including field data. Reviews inspection reports and regulatory correspondence. Shares information with others electronically and drafts response letters. Issues work orders for compliance repairs. Meets with operators and managers to discuss inspection reports. Works with engineer and managers to draft responses.
Coordinates, drafts, and issues any public notices as required working with management, engineering, and staff.
Assists in the resolution or response to compliance.
Prepares and maintains sampling plans including monthly bacteriological, lead and copper, disinfection by-products, and others for all systems and updates sample sites as needed. Ensures all samples are collected and reviews data.
Answers customer inquiries regarding analysis results and distributing copies of results if needed. Provides administrative support to Engineering Department. Processes invoices, copy, route and file documents as needed.
Prepares reports and tracks progress of budgeted project work.
Participates in meetings and other activities of Aqua as required.
Collects data from flow recorder data recorders and pressure recorders. Downloads data to PC and plot data.
Assists in the development of operating and capital budgets. Assists with permit reviews, renewals, and special or new monitoring requirements.
Provides input and assistance with preliminary design, project management, and contractor coordination for compliance-related capital projects, as needed.
Communicate urgent information to supervisors and operators and customers regarding water quality inquiries. Serve in an advisory/training capacity towards plant staff on sampling and proper test procedures to ensure compliance.
Performs other assignments as required.

Knowledge of water distribution systems, leak detection principles, and water loss control concepts preferred.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Develop, review, and maintain high-quality 2D and 3D CAD models and drawings for Geo-Environmental, civil infrastructure projects, ensuring accuracy and compliance with project requirements, Australian standards, and company guidelines.

Manage and process spatial/geospatial data (GIS/CAD) to support design development, analysis, and project documentation workflows.

Career Area

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Caterpillar is developing a new advanced manufacturing campus in Sanford, North Carolina, to expand production capacity for compact track loaders and telehandlers. The modern, technology-enabled operation is expected to incorporate automation, robotics, digital production systems and integrated logistics capabilities to enhance safety, quality and operational performance. Employees will help build the products our customers rely on while developing skills in advanced manufacturing and supporting the continued growth of Caterpillar’s Cat Compact℠ business.

Job Summary

The Environmental, Health and Safety Manager will provide site-level EHS leadership for a new advanced manufacturing facility, helping the site launch safely and build strong operating discipline from the beginning. This leader will be involved from construction planning through startup and stable production. Early priorities will include contractor evaluation related to safety, safety training, contractor safety program adherence, construction risk, site controls and readiness.

This role supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture, where safety is not a checklist or a set of procedures. It requires an EHS leader who can lead through ambiguity, influence project and operations leaders, work directly with contractors and employees, and build a safety culture where safe behavior is coached, expected and reinforced in the flow of daily work.

What You Will Do

Lead EHS execution for a new advanced manufacturing site from construction planning through startup.
Set clear construction-phase safety expectations for contractors, project teams and site leaders, including orientation, site access, work planning, hazard controls, inspections and corrective actions.
Build practical EHS programs, training, audits, reporting routines and risk-reduction processes that support Caterpillar standards, legal requirements and local operating needs.
Partner with construction, facilities, operations, engineering, maintenance, security, human resources, suppliers, contractors and system integrators to identify risks early and resolve issues quickly.
Support safe implementation of advanced manufacturing systems, automated material movement, connected equipment, robotics, energy systems, utilities and production processes.
Establish leader routines for hazard identification, risk assessment, contractor safety, incident response, corrective actions and emergency preparedness.
Use EHS data, leading indicators, inspections, observations, incident trends and audit findings to guide decisions and focus resources where risk is highest.
Provide leadership for environmental compliance, waste management, chemical management, air, water, stormwater, permitting and sustainability-related programs.
Coach leaders and employees, using field observations, feedback, leader routines and follow-up to reinforce safe decisions during construction and startup.

What You Will Have

Environmental Health and Safety Policy Compliance:
Knowledge of environmental, health and safety policies, standards, procedures and legal requirements; ability to lead programs that protect employees, contractors, visitors in a manufacturing environment.

Risk Management:
Knowledge of tools, approaches and practices for identifying, assessing, controlling and monitoring operational, environmental, construction and occupational-health risks before they become incidents.

Decision Making and Critical Thinking:
Ability to analyze technical, operational and compliance data, evaluate alternatives, assess risk and make sound recommendations. Ability to manage multiple priorities while balancing safety, compliance, schedule, cost and operational impact.

Project Management:
Ability to plan, organize, monitor and deliver EHS-related projects, launch activities, corrective actions and readiness plans to scope, schedule and quality expectations. Ability to work with cross-functional teams.

Safety Culture Leadership:
Ability to influence how leaders, employees and contractors think about risk, speak up about hazards, correct unsafe conditions and make safe choices in daily work.

Top Candidates Will Also Have

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health and Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Manufacturing, Construction Management.
Relevant EHS professional certification, such as CSP, ASP, CHMM, CIH, OSHA 30, ISO 14001, ISO 45001 or a comparable credential.
Experience improving EHS performance through both practical processes and behavior-based safety approaches.
Experience supporting construction safety, contractor safety, facility startup, capital projects, commissioning or major operational change.
Experience identifying hazards, assessing risk, implementing controls, investigating incidents and tracking corrective actions.
Strong communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills.

What You Will Get

Launch a new advanced manufacturing operation and shape the EHS foundation from construction through start up.
Lead work that supports Caterpillar’s Safety Driven culture and reinforces that safety is how the work gets done.
Play a visible leadership role in shaping how a new site operates from day one.
Help implement practical EHS systems that support automation, advanced manufacturing, and safe production.

Additional Info

Location: Sanford, North Carolina
Work Arrangement: Onsite, five days per week. Locations may flex between temporary offices while transitioning to new facility.
Travel: High percentage of travel (50-75%) may be required at certain times during construction planning, supplier reviews, equipment installation, commissioning, startup and production ramp-up.

Role Overview

Serves as the Pollution Control Officer (PCO) for the Research compound, overseeing regulatory compliance and permitting activities.
Prepares, processes, and renews environmental and regulatory permits, licenses, and clearances, including but not limited to:
DENR-EMB (e.g., ECC, Discharge Permits, Hazardous Waste Generator ID, PTO, SQI, PMPIN, PCL, CCO)
DOLE (e.g., Permit to Operate, Certificate of Electrical Safety Inspection)
Other agencies: LGUs, BFP, PDEA, PNP, ERC as required

Coordinates with regulatory bodies and government agencies for inspections, compliance audits, and reporting.
Maintains accurate and up-to-date records of permits, inspections, laboratory results and compliance documentation

Oversees environmental performance of the Research Compound including air emissions, wastewater, hazardous and solid waste, and chemical storage and use compliance by:
coordinating environmental monitoring and pollution control activities
monitoring wastewater treatment plant (WWTP/STP) operations
ensuring proper handling, storage and disposal of hazardous substances and chemicals (including development of Chemical Management Plans)
ensuring compliance in the use of PNP and PDEA related controlled chemicals

Prepares, submits and files/documents the following in a timely manner:
Self monitoring reports (SMRs)
Compliance monitoring reports (CMRs)
Priority Chemicals List (PCL) reports
SQI-related chemical consumption reports
waste generation reports
reports that may be required by specific Chemical Control Orders (CCO)
ERC COC report (for Standby generator set)

Conduct orientation and/or coordinates training/learning sessions on environmental compliance for internal stakeholders. Works closely with point persons of Production, Safety, Engineering, CQA&C, MA, R&D, LM and Food Services on integrated compliance practices
Recommend and support implementation of best practices for pollution prevention and sustainability including adaptation to changes in environmental and chemical regulations
Provide necessary support during internal audits, root cause analysis and corrective action planning

Role Qualifications

Graduate of Bachelor's Degree in Chemical Engineering
Working knowledge in environmental compliance or permitting, ideally in a manufacturing or industrial setting - Philippine environmental and chemical safety laws (RA 9275, RA 8749, RA 6969, etc.)
Skilled in preparing SMR, CMR, and related reports
DENR-accredited PCO is an advantage
Strong knowledge of Philippine environmental and chemical safety laws (RA 9275, RA 8749, RA 6969, etc.)
